predecessors.name: Later Zhao
predecessors.text: the city of Ye, where 'Ran Wei usurped the throne of the Later Zhao dynasty' (Ran Wei page); the page gives no extent, drawn as a 100 km disc

successors.name: Former Yan
successors.text: Ye and Xiangguo: the only two cities the pages put in Ran Min's hands (Ran Min's base at Ye; Xiangguo conquered by February 352)

rulers.name: Ran Zhi
rulers.title: crown prince, never took the imperial title

ledger.x: 350: Ran Min takes Ye and proclaims the Wei.
February 352: Ran Min adds Xiangguo and the Shi remnant's land.
5 May 352: Murong Ke marches on Ran Min.
8 September 352: the Wei ends at Ye.

wars.name: Ran Wei-Later Zhao War
wars.outcome: Ran Min besieged Xiangguo in spring 351 and had destroyed the Shi clan and taken it by February 352; Former Yan was asked for aid by Shi Zhi.

wars.name: Conquest of Ran Wei by Former Yan
wars.outcome: Ran Min beaten at Liantai on 17 May 352, executed 1 June; Ye taken 8 September 352 after Jiang Gan's Jin-backed sally of 4 July was routed.

certainty.note: Two years of warfare around Ye: the pages name cities, not a boundary.

sources.title: Conquest of Ran Wei by Former Yan
Ran Wei-Later Zhao War (Battle of Xiangguo, 350-351)
